answer.summary: No credible primary-source evidence was retrieved to support claims about tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams with known perturbations.
answer.content: No peer-reviewed studies or primary-source datasets were found that provide empirical time-series data on output token coherence, decay rates, or state drift in tokenized agents under bounded token budgets and intermittent, perturbed input streams. The investigation confirms the absence of direct, verifiable sources matching the required criteria for comparative analysis with continuous static input baselines. All claims about memory superiority remain ungrounded without such data.
answer.nextTask: Identify and retrieve a peer-reviewed study with explicit time-series metrics on tokenized agent memory retention under intermittent input streams and known perturbations, including per-interval coherence scores and state drift indicators under bounded token budgets. Prioritize studies from arXiv, IEEE Xplore, or ACL Anthology with DOI or stable HTTPS access for verifiable data extraction.
answer.lesson: All claims about agent memory performance must be anchored in direct, verifiable time-series data from peer-reviewed studies with explicit decay and coherence metrics under controlled input conditions before comparative analysis can proceed.
